title: Streaming and Suspense
description: Learn how streaming HTML and Suspense boundaries improve perceived performance for slow data fetches.

data.text: Streaming lets Next.js send parts of the page to the browser as soon as they are ready, instead of waiting for every data source to finish. **Suspense** is React's way of showing a fallback while a piece of content loads.

Together, they solve a common problem: one slow API call should not block the entire page. A dashboard might need user profile data instantly, then recommendations a moment later. Streaming lets the shell appear first, and Suspense lets you replace loading placeholders with real content when it arrives.
How streaming works in App Router

items: The server sends the root layout and fast sections immediately.
Suspense boundaries mark the slow sections.
When a streaming section finishes, React hydrates just that part.
Users see a usable page much sooner than waiting for the full payload.

data.title: Pro tip
data.text: Place Suspense boundaries around independent slow data sources. Do not wrap large parts of the page if the shell and content can load in parallel.

terms.definition: Sending HTML in chunks from the server so the browser can render parts early.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Streaming reduces time-to-first-byte for the shell.
Suspense boundaries let you show placeholders for slow parts.
data.takeaway: Use streaming when your page has mixed-speed data sources. Keep the shell fast and stream the rest.
